               <ns0:head>CHAP. XI.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 ANd it came to pass, when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence, to teach and to preach in their cities.<ns0:note place="bottom">We never find our Saviour idle, but continually going up and down doing good, and we find him most intent upon <ns0:hi>Preaching,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Teaching,</ns0:hi> which doubtless is the great Work of the Ministers of the Gospel, of what quality soever they be, they can pretend to no higher then Christs. Nor did our Saviour think it enough to send others in his stead, as his <ns0:hi>Cu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rates,</ns0:hi> he went himself. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> noteth <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10.1. that <ns0:hi>he sent the</ns0:hi> 70, <ns0:hi>two by two into every City,</ns0:hi> whither himself was to follow, so as it seems, he did not judge it enough, that one Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clamation of the Gospel should be made to them. For those that think there is a Distinction to be made betwixt <ns0:hi>Preaching,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Teaching</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> and <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> they may learn from this Text, that they are both the Works of Christs Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters, if they be bound to take Example from their Masters, and not think the Servant is above his Lord. Those that un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dervalue <ns0:hi>Preaching,</ns0:hi> as the least part of the Ministerial Work, do both forget this Text, and what <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> said, that Christ sent him <ns0:hi>not to Baptize, but to Preach the Gospel.</ns0:hi> That is, not so much to <ns0:hi>Baptize,</ns0:hi> as to <ns0:hi>Preach.</ns0:hi> If any think, that People are now so instructed, that there is no such need of Preaching, they should do well to question their People a little, and they may discover their own great mistakes. Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sides, that Experience teacheth us, that those who are best in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />structed, are most desirous of that which deserveth the Name of <ns0:hi>Preaching,</ns0:hi> which lets us know that there is yet something further to be known, or that we had need have our re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />membrance stirred up, or at least our Affections quick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And said unto him, art thou he that should come? or do we look for another?<ns0:note place="bottom">The instance of this Text alone, is enough to convince the observing Reader of holy Writ, that the Evangelists do not set down all things in that order, as they were done. We have heard nothing before of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>'s being cast into Prison in this Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel, nor do we hear any thing here of the Story of it, till <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 14.6. when our Evangelist occasionally relateth it something largely. He here tells us of something done during his Imprisonment, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>sending two of his Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples to Christ,</ns0:hi> to be satisfyed, whether he was the <ns0:hi>promised Messias,</ns0:hi> or they must look for another. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> reports the same thing, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 19. Could he that was sent before Christ to <ns0:hi>prepare his way,</ns0:hi> and that had <ns0:hi>Baptized him,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>seen the Spirit descending</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> and heard the Voice from Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, saying. <ns0:hi>This is my <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>eloved Son, in whom I am well pleased,</ns0:hi> and who had shewed <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> to his Disciples, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.29.30, 31, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> doubt whether he was the <ns0:hi>Messiah?</ns0:hi> Un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />doubtedly no, but <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> saw how some of his Disc<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ples ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther envying for his sake, as <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.26. or else inclinable to the Common error of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> about the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> were something shaken with the Clamours of the <ns0:hi>Scribes,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees</ns0:hi> (who were far more favourable to <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> then to <ns0:hi>Christ.</ns0:hi>) That they might be satisfyed from their own sight of the Works of Christ, he a little before his Death sendeth them to Christ on this Errand, <ns0:hi>Art thou he who should come</ns0:hi> (in the Greek, <ns0:hi>who is coming</ns0:hi>) which lets us know the full Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pectation the Jews generally had at that time of a <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> coming. They desire only to be satisfyed whether Christ was he.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 Jesus answered, and said unto them, Go, and shew John again those things which ye do hear, and see.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 29<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached unto them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And blessed is he whosoever shall not be of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fended in me.<ns0:note place="bottom">We must imagine these Disciples of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> to have staid with Christ some time, and to have seen him work some of these Miracles, and to have heard him Preach, and seen the great suc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cess of his Ministry, and then to have lest him with this An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> therefore addeth <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.21. <ns0:hi>And in that same Hour he cured many of their Infirmities, and Plagues, and of Evil Spirits, and unto many that were Blind, he gave sight.</ns0:hi> Then he repeateth the Answer which we have here, in which our Saviour referreth unto his Works, as sufficiently testifying of him, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.36.37. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.25.37, 38<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> we read not that these Disciples saw any dead Person raised, whilst they were with Christ, but it appeareth from <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 7.18, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> that the report of such a Miracle, was the occasion of their coming to Christ. The question is, how the sight of these things done by our Saviour, could be a sufficient Argument to confirm to them that he was the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi>? Especially con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sidering that his <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> did the same things. Answer. First it was Prophesied by <ns0:hi>Isaiah, Ch.</ns0:hi> 35.4, 5, 6. That when God <ns0:hi>should come to save them, the Eyes of the Blind should be opened, and the Ears of the Deaf unstopped, then shall the Lame Man leap as an Hart, and the Tongue of the Dumb sing,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 61.1. That the <ns0:hi>Messiah should Preach good Tidings to the Meek,</ns0:hi> that is, the Poor, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 4.18. which Christ <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. applyed to himself. So that the fulfilling of these promises argued, that the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> was come, and no other was to be looked for, whether these things were done by him, or by his Disciples. Secondly, <ns0:hi>The Disciples as yet had done no such things,</ns0:hi> so as his doing of them plain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Evidenced his Divine Power, the others did them but as his Disciples, by his Power and Authority. 3. It is more then probable, <ns0:hi>that when the Disciples did them,</ns0:hi> they used <ns0:hi>some such</ns0:hi> Form as <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> used, <ns0:hi>Acts.</ns0:hi> 3.6. <ns0:hi>In the Name of Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus Christ of Nazareth, arise and walk</ns0:hi>; we find <ns0:hi>Peter v.</ns0:hi> 12. very wary, that the People should not mistake in thinking, they did it by their own Power or Holiness. <ns0:hi>And the Poor have the Gospel Preached to them.</ns0:hi> Gr. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which may be Translated, <ns0:hi>The Poor Preach the Gospel</ns0:hi> in an Active Sense, as the Word is used, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 2.10. or the <ns0:hi>Poor are Gospelized.</ns0:hi> Taking the Word in a <ns0:hi>passive Sense,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 4.2. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.25. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 4.6. In the passive Sense it may be understood either of a more External Reception of the Gospel upon Preaching, or of a more <ns0:hi>Internal Reception</ns0:hi> of the Gospel by Faith. In all Senses it was true, of the times of the <ns0:hi>Messiah: The Poor Preached the Gospel</ns0:hi>; nor was this a mean Evidence, that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> was come to see a few poor Fisher-men, at his Call leaving their Nets and their Friends, and following one calling them, to Preach a new Doctrine to the World. 2. <ns0:hi>The Poor had the Gospel Preached to them,</ns0:hi> nor was this a less Evidence of Christ, to be the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sidering the Prophecy, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 61.1. and the contempt of the Poor amongst the Jews. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 7.49. But that the Poor, who commonly are the more ignorant, and rude sort of Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple should Vouchsafe to <ns0:hi>hear the Gospel,</ns0:hi> and be turned into the <ns0:hi>likeness of the Gospel</ns0:hi> upon Christ's Preaching to them, this was yet an higher Evidence. Many by <ns0:hi>Poor</ns0:hi> understand the <ns0:hi>Poor in Spirit.</ns0:hi> The binding up of broken Hearts, and bringing glad Tidings to Souls sadded on Spiritual accounts, is a great effect of the Divine Power. It followeth, <ns0:hi>And blessed is he who shall not be offended in me.</ns0:hi> It is not im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />probable that our Saviour here reflecteth on the Disciples of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> who out of a great Honour for their <ns0:hi>Master,</ns0:hi> took ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny occasions to be offended at Christ. One while because <ns0:hi>he, and his Disciples<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> did not fast so often, as they and the Phari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sees,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9. <ns0:hi>v,</ns0:hi> 14. another while because so many fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed him, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.26. But the Words spoken have a fur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther reference, then to <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Disciples. The Lord Jesus and his Doctrine are to many a <ns0:hi>Stone of stumbling,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Rock of offence,</ns0:hi> according to the Prophecie, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 8.14. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 28.16. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 2.34. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.33. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.23. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.6. The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> stumbled at the meanness of his Person, and Parentage, and the meanness of his Followers. The <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> not at these things only, but his Ignominious Death. At this day many stumble at the <ns0:hi>Sublimeness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>strictness of his Doctrine,</ns0:hi> &c. Christ speaks here with reference to all, and pronoun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceth that man, a <ns0:hi>Blessed man, who shall so take Offence at nothing,</ns0:hi> whether respecting his <ns0:hi>Person,</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Life,</ns0:hi> or his <ns0:hi>Death,</ns0:hi> his <ns0:hi>Doctrine,</ns0:hi> or his <ns0:hi>Followers,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>to deter, or dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />courage him from embracing him,</ns0:hi> and believing in him as the Saviour of lost Sinners, that shall by Faith receive him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:236" />7 And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see, A reed shaken with the wind?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft rayment? Behold, they that wear soft clothing are in Kings houses.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 But what went ye out for to see? A pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet? Yea I say unto you, and more than a pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> repeating the same Story, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.24.25. instead of <ns0:hi>they that are clothed in soft Rayment,</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>They that are Gorgeously apparelled,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Live delicately, are in Kings houses.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour here doth tacitly imply, that the Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters of the Gospel, should neither be incertain, and incon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stant Men: Nor yet delicate Men, affecting splendid Ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />parel, or delicate Diet, but minding their great work, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Revelation of the Will of God.</ns0:hi> But the Scope of his present Speech here, was to confirm the multitude in their good Opinion of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> and to keep them from being Scan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dalized, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or altering their Opinion of him, because he was now in Prison. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 14.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 21.26. <ns0:hi>All men held Iohn as a Prophet.</ns0:hi> You went out (saith our <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi>) into the Wilderness to hear <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> Preach, you did not go out to see some idle Light-man, such as a Reed shaken with the Wind. Nor yet to see a Man clothed Gorgeously (the Wilderness is no place for such Persons, they are to be found in the Courts, and Palaces of Princes) you went out to hear one revealing the Will of God to you. Nor did you mistake. He was a <ns0:hi>Prophet.</ns0:hi> Not <ns0:hi>that Prophet,</ns0:hi> of which <ns0:hi>Moses spake, Deut.</ns0:hi> 18.15. But <ns0:hi>a Prophet.</ns0:hi> Yea, and more than a <ns0:hi>Prophet.</ns0:hi> One that hath taught you, what none of the Prophets ever could teach you. That I, the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> am come, they could only tell you,<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that I should come.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 For this is he of whom it is written, Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Verily I say unto you, amongst them that are born of women, there hath not arisen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven, is greater than he.<ns0:note place="bottom">St. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.27, 28. only he saith, <ns0:hi>There hath not arisen a greater Prophet, than Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> It was written, <ns0:hi>Malachy</ns0:hi> 3.1. <ns0:hi>Behold I will send my Messenger before my Face, and he shall prepare the way before me. And the Lord whom you seek, shall suddenly come to his Temple, even the Messenger of the Covenant, whom you delight in. Behold, he shall come, saith the Lord of Hosts.</ns0:hi> The latter part was a Prophecy of <ns0:hi>Christ.</ns0:hi> The former part, a Prophecy of <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> and applied to him not in this Text only, but <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.2. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.76. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 7.27. Christ is set out as a great Prince, who sends his Harbingers be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore him to <ns0:hi>prepare his way,</ns0:hi> and by <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Preaching we may learn the Ministers Duty, who are to <ns0:hi>prepare Christ's way</ns0:hi> to peoples Souls, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> To Preach <ns0:hi>Repentance</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Faith in Christ. Verily I say unto you, amongst those that are born of Women, there hath not arisen a greater</ns0:hi>: That is, (as <ns0:hi>Luke expounds it</ns0:hi>) a <ns0:hi>greater Prophet. i. e.</ns0:hi> Amongst all the <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Old Testament,</ns0:hi> God raised up none greater than <ns0:hi>Iohn. But he that is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.</ns0:hi> Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> and many others think that by this Phrase is to be understood, the least of those who shall Preach the Gospel after my Resurrection, will be greater than he, that is, as to their Doctrine. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> could only declare me to be come. They shall Preach me, as having died for my Peoples Sins, and risen again for <ns0:hi>their justification<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Rom.</ns0:hi> 4.25. The Death, and the Resurrection of Christ, were indeed great Points of the Gospel, which <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> could only Prophecy of, not Preach of, and declare us things in his time accomplished.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>is got<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ten by Force, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nd that they that thrust men.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> suffereth vio<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lence, and the violent take it by force <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 16.16.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note place="bottom">As <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptist</ns0:hi> was a great man, so the Lord hath own<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed him as such giving such a Success to his Ministry, that ever since he began the Course of it, men have been carried on with a great Ardor, and Heat, in hearing and receiving the Gospel, which is the Gospel of the Kingdom, and bringeth men into the Kingdom of Christ amongst men, and at last to the Kingdom of Glory. The Hearts of Men and Women have been inflamed with a Desire after the knowledge, and obtaining of Heaven, and Heavenly things: They are great Persons whom God thus owneth, and those whom the Lord thus owneth, are ordinarily such as have some measures of the Spirit of this first Gospel Ministry, making the great things of God the matter of their Discourse, and doing their Work, with a Seriousness, Zeal, and Favour fitted to it. <ns0:hi>The violent take it by Force:</ns0:hi> They are not lazy Wishes, or Cold indeavours that will bring men to Heaven.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 For all the prophets, and the law prophe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cied until John.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is no wonder, that there was such an heat kindled in the Souls of People, upon <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptists</ns0:hi> coming, for they understood that Christ typified in the Law, and only foretold by the Prophets, was now come. So as the <ns0:hi>Cere<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monial Law</ns0:hi> from his time began to dye, and all the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phecies of Christ in the Prophets, began then to have their Complement. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> shewed them with his Finger, him who before had been only darkly revealed under Types and Fi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gures, and in the Prophecies of the <ns0:hi>Prophets</ns0:hi>: Men came to see that they had not hoped, or waited in vain for the Sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> [<ns0:hi>Prophecied</ns0:hi>] in this Verse, signifies <ns0:hi>made dark Revelations</ns0:hi> of Christ, and the Kingdom of Heaven.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And if ye will receive <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> this is Elias which was for to come.<ns0:note place="bottom">God had told the <ns0:hi>Iews, Mal.</ns0:hi> 4, 5, 6. that <ns0:hi>he would send them Flijah the Prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord. And he shall turn the Hearts of the Fathers to the Children, and the Hearts of the Children to the Fathers, lest</ns0:hi> (saith he) <ns0:hi>I come and smite the Earth with a Curse.</ns0:hi> This Prophecy related to <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> as our Saviour here teacheth us, so <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.17. it is confirmed by the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Zachariah,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 9.11. From which last Text it appeareth, that the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> had a Tradition, that <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> should come before the <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi> Their mistake was that they looked for an <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> to come in Person, when as God meant no more (as the <ns0:hi>Angel</ns0:hi> expoundeth it, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 1.17.) than one <ns0:hi>in the Spirit,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Power of Elias,</ns0:hi> as bold and free a Preacher, who should no more fear the Face of Men, in the discharge of his Duty, than <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> did (saith our Saviour) if you will believe, this <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was that <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Prophecied of by <ns0:hi>Malachy.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rev. 2.7, 11, 17, 29. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 3.6, 13, 22.</ns0:note> He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is an <ns0:hi>Epiphonema</ns0:hi> or Conclusion often used by our Saviour (and by St. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Revelation</ns0:hi>) quickening up the hearers to a just Attention to, and belief of, what in the Doctrine preceding he had revealed to them: Intimating that he knew, that what he had said would not be enter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tained, or believed of all, but only of such, whose Ears and Hearts God had opened, or should open to receive spiritual Mysteries. But it was a matter of great Concernment, he therefore calls upon those, whose Ears God had opened to attend to it. So <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 13.9, 43. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 4.9. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 7.16. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 8.8.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children, sitting in the markets, and calling to their fellows.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And saying we have piped to you, and ye have not danced, we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> telling to us the same History, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31, 32, 33, 34, 35. prefaceth it thus, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29, 30. <ns0:hi>And all the People that heard him, and the Publicans justified God, being Bapti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zed with the Baptism of Iohn. But the Pharisees, and the Lawyers rejected the Counsel of God against themselves, being not Baptized of him.</ns0:hi> Which letteth us know that our Saviour by the term [<ns0:hi>this Generation</ns0:hi>] here doth not mean all the People of that <ns0:hi>Generation:</ns0:hi> But the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Lawyers,</ns0:hi> whom nothing could allure, or perswade to the receiving of Jesus Christ, neither the Ministry, and Example of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> nor yet his own Preaching and Example. For the People and the Publicans, justified the words of Christ, which he had spoken in Commendation of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> and were Baptized of him: But the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lawyers</ns0:hi> did not believe, nor would be Baptized of him. These our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour likens to a Company of sullen Children, whom their Fellows could not perswade any way to a Compliance with them: If they Piped they would not Dance, if they sang to them some mournful Songs, neither would they be affected with them, so as no Tune would please them. It is thought, that our Saviour doth here allude to some sport used then amongst Children, which we are not so well acquainted with, wherein Children were wont to sing, sometimes more Mer<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y and Pleasant, sometimes more sad and mournful Songs one to another: And that he here likeneth the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lawyers</ns0:hi> to a sullen set of Children, that let their Compa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nions sing what they would, would not answer them. Our Saviours meaning is expounded plainly enough by the next words.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:237" />18 For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a devil.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 The Son of man came eating, and drink<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, and they say, behold, a man gluttonous, and a wine bibber, a friend of publicanes and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath the same words. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33.34, 35. The Sense of the Words is this, God hath by his Providence used all means to win this People to the Gospel. The Doctrine of <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi> was the same, but their Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per and Converse was very different: <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was an Au<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tere and Morose man, Christ was of a more free, and <ns0:hi>familia<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Conversation:</ns0:hi> But these men would ne<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ther give the one, nor the other a good word. They <ns0:hi>reviled</ns0:hi> both of them, and <ns0:hi>rejected</ns0:hi> them both, and the Doctrine which they brought. <ns0:hi>Iohn came neither Eating nor Drinking,</ns0:hi> that is, not as other men ordinarily do, he was a Man that lived most in the Wilderness, and fed upon very ordinary Diet, not <ns0:hi>Eat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>Publicanes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sinners,</ns0:hi> not coming at any Feasts, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and they said of him, <ns0:hi>He hath a Devil</ns0:hi>; he is a Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lancholick, Hypocondriack fellow, a kind of a Mad-man. <ns0:hi>The Son of Man came Eating and Drinking,</ns0:hi> he was of a more affable pleasant Temper, of a more Free, and less re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />served Converse, Eating, and Drinking as other men (tho keeping to the Law of <ns0:hi>Temperance</ns0:hi>) such things as the Countrey afforded, not refusing to be present at Fea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> tho Publicanes and Sinners were there. They said to him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold a Man gluttonous, a Wine bibber, a Friend of Publi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cans and Sinnes:</ns0:hi> He displeased them with the too great Freedom of his Conversation, from whence by the way they may be better instructed) who place some <ns0:hi>Perfection,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Merit,</ns0:hi> in living like <ns0:hi>Monks</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Hermits</ns0:hi>; by that rule <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> was to be preferred before <ns0:hi>Christ.</ns0:hi>) But Christ could please the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Lawyers,</ns0:hi> and their followers no more than <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> did. They could not say, he was Melancholick or Morose; but they Blasphemed him to an higher Degree, calling him a <ns0:hi>Glutton,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Drunkard,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Friend</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Publicans</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sinners.</ns0:hi> A Godly man let his Temper and Converse be what it will, pleaseth none, who hateth the Truth of the Gospel, and the Power of Godliness. If he be reserved, then he is a Morose, Melan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cholick man: If he be of a more Free and open Converse, then he is a <ns0:hi>Drunkard,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Glutton,</ns0:hi> something or other they must have to say against a Man, that will not run with them to the same <ns0:hi>Excess of Riot</ns0:hi>; tho they lay to their Charge, things that they know not. The business is, they hate the Power of Godliness in them. This instance of these Mens thus treating <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> is of mighty use to strengthen those who meet with the very same things. <ns0:hi>But Wisdom is justified of her Children.</ns0:hi> There is a great Variety amongst Interpreters, in giving the Sense of these words. Some think them spoken <ns0:hi>Ironically,</ns0:hi> for the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> went for the Children of Wisdom. Some think them spoken plainly, and think it should be <ns0:hi>Wisdom</ns0:hi> is judged, or <ns0:hi>Condemned</ns0:hi> of her Children; but tho the word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifying to <ns0:hi>Iustice</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>do Iustice to</ns0:hi> another, which accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to the Merit, or Demerit of the Person may be, by <ns0:hi>justi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fying,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>condemning,</ns0:hi> upon which Account it was true here, that Wisdom was condemned of those who pretended to be her Children, and the word is so used in other Authors; yet we have no such usage of it in Scripture. Not to reckon the various Senses others put upon the words. The plain Sense of them seems to be this. It is a proverbial Speech, something like that, <ns0:hi>Ars non habet inimicum praeter igno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rantem.</ns0:hi> Learning hath no Enemies, but the Ignorant. I <ns0:hi>who am the Wisdom of God, am justified by you,</ns0:hi> who truly believe on me: You know I am no Glutton, no Wine-bibber, no Friend of Publicans and Sinners. 2. Or, <ns0:hi>Grace is justified of all that are partakers of it.</ns0:hi> Godly men that are wise, will own the Grace of God in all men, whether they be of <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Temper, or of mine, whether of more Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stere<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or more pleasant Tempers: Or, 3. <ns0:hi>The wise Councel of God, making use of several Instruments of several Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pers,</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>win these People unto his Gospel will be justified,</ns0:hi> that is, acquitted, defended, praised<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> adored of <ns0:hi>those who be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />long unto God,</ns0:hi> and are acquainted with his Wisdom and Councels: <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, The people <ns0:hi>justified God, Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.29. Some by <ns0:hi>the Children of Wisdom,</ns0:hi> understand the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> themselves (who thought themselves the Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren of Wisdom) or the Generality of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who were <ns0:hi>Condemned</ns0:hi> in their ow<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Consciences, and could not but in Heart<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>justifie Christ, tho in their Speeches they condemned him. But Christ never called them the <ns0:hi>Children of Wisdom.</ns0:hi> This interpretation therefore seemeth something strained. That which seemeth the most natural, is what I before hinted. Tho those that pretend to be the Children of Wisdom, thus speak of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> and of me; yet those who are truly wise will justifie me, and also the Councels and Wisdom of my Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther in the use of all means, to bring them to receive the glad Tidings of Salvation, brought to them both by my more Austere, and reserved forerunner, and by my self, who have chosen, tho an Holy and unblameable, yet a more Free, and pleasant way of Converse with them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 10.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> Then began he to upbraid the cities, where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Lord had hitherto spent most of his time in <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> and the Cities belonging to that Province, there both <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> and himself had preached the Gospel, there be had wrought many Miracles, by both aiming at their <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pentance,</ns0:hi> but there were multitudes that did not receive him, nor would be brought to any sight of their sins, or any acknowledgment of him as the <ns0:hi>Messias.</ns0:hi> He now begins to reprove them smartly, not that they did not applaud, and commend him, but because they did not <ns0:hi>Repent.</ns0:hi> This was Christ's and in all his Preaching, and in all his miraculous Operations, to bring men to <ns0:hi>Repentance,</ns0:hi> and to receive him as the <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> and this should be the great end pursued by all his Ministers.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Wo unto thee, Chorazin, wo unto thee, Bethsaida, for if the mighty works which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 But I say unto you, It shall be more tole<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, than for you.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 13, 14. <ns0:hi>Chorazin</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Bethsaida,</ns0:hi> were two Cities of <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> not far from one ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, only the Lake of <ns0:hi>Gennesaret</ns0:hi> was betwixt them, <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pernaum</ns0:hi> (by and by spoken of,) was betwixt them both, on the same side of the Lake, as <ns0:hi>Bethsaida,</ns0:hi> which was the City of <ns0:hi>Phillip, Andrew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Peter, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.44. In these Towns Christ had often Preached, so probably had the A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postles, and Christ had done many great works in them. <ns0:hi>Tyre and Sidon,</ns0:hi> were Habitations of Heathens, their Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try joyned to <ns0:hi>Galilee.</ns0:hi> They were places of great Traffick, inhabited with <ns0:hi>Canaanitish</ns0:hi> Idolaters, and exceedingly wicked, threatned by the Prophet <ns0:hi>Isaiah, Ch.</ns0:hi> 23. and by the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet <ns0:hi>Ezekiel, Ch.</ns0:hi> 26. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 27, <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 28, and by <ns0:hi>Amos, Ch.</ns0:hi> 1.9. a People odious to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> upon many Accounts. To these our Lord here compareth the <ns0:hi>Galileans,</ns0:hi> telling them, that they were worse than that <ns0:hi>Pagan</ns0:hi> People, who were so Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />temptible in their Eyes, and that their Plagues in the day of Judgment, would be greater. For (saith he) <ns0:hi>If the mighty Works which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in Sackcloth and Ashes.</ns0:hi> Some think this a strong Proof. That where the Gospel is Preached, God gives a sufficiency of Grace: So as if men will but use that Power, which they have in their own Wills, they may with the Assistance only of that Grace truly repent, and be saved. I shall not meddle with that Dispute; but cannot see how that Notion, can derive any Proof from this Text, 1. <ns0:hi>Because the Text only men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioneth Christs Miracles, not his Preaching.</ns0:hi> 2. The Text doth not say, they would long ago have repented unto Life, but they would have <ns0:hi>repented in Sackcloth and Ashes,</ns0:hi> they would have been more affected then these <ns0:hi>Galileans</ns0:hi> were, who shewed no Sense at all of their sins. The <ns0:hi>King</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Nineveh</ns0:hi> and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s People repented, <ns0:hi>Ionah</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 7, 8. So did <ns0:hi>Ahab,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 21.27. yet none will say, they repented unto Life. None ever denied a <ns0:hi>Power in Mans Will,</ns0:hi> (his understanding being by the Gospel inlightned to his Duty) to perform Acts of <ns0:hi>Moral Discipline.</ns0:hi> 3. Our Saviour might here speak after the manner of Men according to rational Conjectures, and Probabilities. The Scope of our Saviour in these words is to be attended, which was only to shew, that the Men of <ns0:hi>Ce<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />razin</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Bethsaida,</ns0:hi> shewing no signs of Remorse for sin, or Conviction, of the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> upon the sight of his Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cles, confirming his Doctrine to be from Heaven, had shewed a greater Stubbornness, and hardness of Heart than these Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thens, who tho they were bad enough, yet had not had such means to reform, and to convince them. Therefore he tel's them their place in Hell, would be more dreadful than the place of the Men of <ns0:hi>Tyre</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sidon.</ns0:hi> And so we are by this Text taught, That as the sins of Men, who have the Light of the Gospel are much greater, than the sins of the worst of Men, who have it not: So their Condemnation in the day of Judgment will be much heavier, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.19.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And thou Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shall be brought down to hell, for if the mighty works which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mained unto this day.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of Judgment then for thee.<ns0:note place="bottom">This Speech of our Saviour is much of the same import with the other. The Scope, and Sence of it the same, to let the <ns0:hi>Capernaites</ns0:hi> know that the hardness of their Heart, was greater in contempt of the Gospel, confirmed by so many mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />raculous Operations, and their guilt greater, than the guilt of <ns0:hi>Sodom,</ns0:hi> long since destroyed by <ns0:hi>Fire and Brimstone, Gen.</ns0:hi> 18. for tho they were guilty of Prodigious Sinning, yet they had not such means to Convince, Reclaim, and Reform them God had not sent his <ns0:hi>Son</ns0:hi> amongst them, nor given them such Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimonies of that Act of Grace, as he had given these, by Vouchsafing, to confirm the Doctrine of his Son by Miracles, and therefore they must expect, that God in the Day of Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, should deal more severely with them, than with the fil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thy, and impure <ns0:hi>Sodomites.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour here speaketh not as an all-knowing God, but as the Son of Man to the <ns0:hi>Sons</ns0:hi> of Men, who speak upon Probabilities, and rational Conjectures. If we should say that Christ spake this as an all-knowing God, all that can be inferred, is this, That an External Reformation, may be a <ns0:hi>lengthening out of Persons Tranquillity,</ns0:hi> in the mean time God was just to both, in not giving them such means, they Sinning Notoriously against the Light of Nature, which they had, and the <ns0:hi>Light</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Lots</ns0:hi> holy Example, whose Righteous Soul they vexed with their filthy Conversation, and unrighte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous deeds, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.7, 8. and he was also just in destroying of them. <ns0:hi>Capernaum</ns0:hi> is here said to have <ns0:hi>been exalted to Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven,</ns0:hi> either with respect to their <ns0:hi>Trading</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>outward Prospe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity,</ns0:hi> or with respect to the <ns0:hi>means of Grace,</ns0:hi> they enjoyed in hearing Christs Sermons, and seeing his Miracles. The <ns0:hi>cast<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing down to Hell</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. seems to be meant of a Temporal Destruction, the Word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> not signifying the place of the Damned, but the State of the dead, but <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 22. must be understood of <ns0:hi>Eternal Condemnation,</ns0:hi> which shall be <ns0:hi>in the Day of Iudgment.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:237" />25 At that time Jesus answered, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 2.8.</ns0:note> hid these things from the wise, and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Even so, father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 10. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. hath the same thing, only he thus prefaceth. <ns0:hi>In that hour Iesus rejoyced in Spirit,</ns0:hi> and said, <ns0:hi>I thank thee, O Father, Lord of Heaven and Earth,</ns0:hi> &c. He rejoyced in Spirit, his Heart was inwardly affected with this Grace of God his Father. Then <ns0:hi>He answered, and said.</ns0:hi> Answering in Scripture doth not always signifie, replying to the Words of others, but a speaking, upon some fit oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casion offered, a beginning of a Speech. <ns0:hi>I thank thee, O Father! Lord of Heaven and Earth.</ns0:hi> In the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> the same Word is used, which signifyeth to <ns0:hi>Confess.</ns0:hi> In all Thanks-giving, and Praising, there is a Confession of the Power, Wisdom, or Goodness of God, so as all praising is a <ns0:hi>Confessing,</ns0:hi> tho all <ns0:hi>Confession</ns0:hi> be not praising: By calling his Father <ns0:hi>Lord of Heaven and Earth,</ns0:hi> he acknowledgeth his ab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />solute Power to have done otherwise, even as it pleased him. <ns0:hi>Because thou hast hid these things, from the Wise and Pru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dent.</ns0:hi> By the Wise, and Prudent, he here plainly means the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Learned Doctors</ns0:hi> of that Age, who should have been Wise, and Prudent, and were so, both in their own, and in their Followers opinion. By <ns0:hi>these things,</ns0:hi> he means the Mysteries of the Gospel, as <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 13.11. <ns0:hi>The Mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven.</ns0:hi> God is said to have <ns0:hi>hid them,</ns0:hi> because he had not revealed them to them, nor can it be understood of a meer <ns0:hi>External Revelation</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> by the Preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of the Gospel, but of an <ns0:hi>Internal Revelation</ns0:hi> by his Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit, so as they embraced, and believed them, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.10. in which Sense <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> saith, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.3. <ns0:hi>If our Gospel be hid, it is hid to them that perish. And hast revealed them to Babes.</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. It signifieth Persons that are <ns0:hi>Young</ns0:hi> in years [Infants] and weak in Understaning. He Principally means his <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> together with those ordinary Persons that believed in him, for <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 7.48.49. the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> said, <ns0:hi>Have any of the Rulers, or the Pharisees, believed on him? But this People who know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth not the Law are Cursed.</ns0:hi> O Father (saith our Saviour) thou hast all Power in thine Hand, thou art the Lord of Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven and Earth, thou couldest by thy Spirit, have caused these Learned Men to have received, and Imbraced thy Gospel, and followed me, as well as these poor Fisher-men, and other Jews of none of the highest quality; in that thou hast not done it, thou hast declared thy Justice, for their rejecting of thy Counsel, for their Salvation, but in that thou hast revealed these things to any, especially to these Persons, not under the same Worldly advantages, for Reputation, Wisdom, and Wit. Herein thou hast shewed thy special, and abounding Grace, as well as the greatness of thy Power. Lord!
